title: SQL LIKE Operator
text:
SQL
LIKE
Operator



The SQL LIKE Operator

The
LIKE
operator is used in a
WHERE
clause to search for a specified pattern within a column's text
data.

There are two wildcards often used in conjunction with the
LIKE
operator:

A percent sign
%
- represents zero, one, or multiple characters

A underscore sign
_
- represents a single character

The following SQL selects all customers that starts with "a":

Syntax

SELECT
column1, column2, ...
FROM
table_name
WHERE
columnN
LIKE
pattern
;

The % Wildcard

The
%
wildcard represents any number of characters, even zero characters.

The _ Wildcard

The
_
wildcard represents one single character.

It can be any character or number, but each
_
represents one, and only one, character.

Starts With

To return records that starts with a specific letter or phrase, add the
%
at the end of the letter or phrase.

Tip:
You can also combine any number of conditions using
AND
or
OR
operators.

Ends With

To return records that ends with a specific letter or phrase, add the
%
at the beginning of the letter or phrase.

Tip:
You can also combine "starts with" and "ends with":

Contains

To return records that contains a specific letter or phrase, add the

%
both before and after the letter or phrase.

Combine Wildcards

Any wildcard, like
%
and
_

, can be used in combination with other
wildcards.

Without Wildcards

If no wildcard is specified, the phrase has to have an exact match to return a result.
